ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal ground line, and near the same point P on the ground are the landing points of two dashed-line horizontal-projectile trajectories; the small ball a at a higher position on the left has an initial-velocity arrow horizontally to the right and falls along the dashed line to P; the small ball b at a lower position on the right has an initial-velocity arrow horizontally to the left and also falls along the dashed line to P. The problem statement also explains that the horizontal distances from point P to the two balls' throwing points are equal, and that the throwing height of ball a is higher than that of ball b. Then reason: Let the common horizontal distance from the two balls to point P be x, and the throwing heights be h_a and h_b respectively, with h_a>h_b. The falling time of horizontal projectile motion is determined by the vertical direction, t=√(2h/g), so t_a>t_b. The magnitude of the horizontal initial velocity is v_0=x/t, and the magnitude of the vertical component of velocity when landing is v_y=gt. The angle θ between the direction of the landing velocity and the horizontal direction of the initial velocity satisfies tanθ=v_y/v_0=gt/(x/t)=gt^2/x=2h/x. Because h_a>h_b, tanθ_a>tanθ_b; within the range from 0 to 90 degrees, the larger tanθ is, the larger θ is. Therefore θ_a>θ_b.
